newsitem.title: KUWAIT: OPEC expected to roll over ceiling - Kuwait source.
newsitem.headline: OPEC expected to roll over ceiling - Kuwait source.

text.p: OPEC is expected to roll over its oil production ceiling when the group meets later this month, Kuwaiti oil industry sources said on Wednesday.
But if the issue of higher quotas is raised Kuwait will reiterate its long held demands for an extra 200,000 barrels per day (bpd), the sources said.
"It depends on the atmosphere and the benefit of OPEC," said one source when asked if Kuwait had decided to demand a higher quota at OPEC's next meeting on November 27 in Vienna.
"But I do not think that it is in OPEC's interest to raise the ceiling now and I think it will be rolled over," said the source who is familiar with official thinking.

"We have a legitimate claim to increase our production quota by 200,000 barrels per day and if raising the (OPEC) ceiling is discussed (at the ministerial meeting), we, like others, will ask for a higher quota," the source said.
Delegates and some ministers from most of OPEC's 11 members have said they favoured maintaining the 25.03 million bpd ceiling until the middle of 1997.
Some Kuwait industry sources say a higher OPEC ceiling could depress world oil prices.
"Then we will make the same revenue from 2.2 million bpd as we are making now from two million bpd," said one source.
Other official sources are concerned about Kuwait's market share at a time when other OPEC members are overproducing.
"There is a demand growth and we think that we have to protect our market share," one Kuwaiti source said.
"It is no secret that OPEC is overproducing and we have to defend our market share...We deserve a higher quota."
According to a Reuters survey, OPEC wellhead crude output in September was about 25.86 million bpd, about 800,000 bpd over the ceiling.
Kuwait, which has an OPEC quota of two million bpd, says its production capacity currently stands at 2.5 million bpd.
